newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former PM Hata quits main Japan opposition party.
newsitem.headline: Former PM Hata quits main Japan opposition party.

text.p: Former prime minister Tsutomu Hata will leave Japan's main opposition party to form his own group, he said on Monday, after marathon negotiations failed to keep him in the fold.
Hata said he would leave Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) to form his own party and launch it within the year. He spoke at a joint news conference with Shinshinto President Ichiro Ozawa.

Hata chose to exit the party after failing in three meetings over five days to narrow his differences with Ozawa, a longtime ally, over how best to oppose Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).

The departure of a key founding member was the latest blow to the two-year-old party, a blend of nine smaller groups, which has seen factional tensions rise in the wake of a poor showing in general elections in October.

Some 10 of Shinshinto's 156 lower house lawmakers were expected to follow Hata into his new party, which he was expected to register before the end of the year in order to qualify for government subsidies, political sources said.
Hata indicated he would continue cooperating with Shinshinto and seek alliances with reform-minded opposition parties such as the Democratic Party.

Both Hata and Ozawa were senior members of the LDP but left in 1993 to form the precursor to Shinshinto. Hata led a minority coalition government that lasted only two months before collapsing in June 1994.
